academicJudgment.claim: The confirmed comparative national politics and public governance and empirical-methods core supports two meaningful broader UCR responses, while the revised-cohort final-year theory and research culmination remains outside the assessed scope.
academicJudgment.basis: Actual comparative politics, political theory, international relations, public/international law and quantitative/qualitative inquiry supply sustained political substance. The first option prioritises comparative/public-policy and data inquiry. The second retains a substantive comparative/legal/economic/methods core while adding real rhetorical, stylistic, media and AI-ethics inquiry to the specific communication generators.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: General law/economics/communication coherence would not suffice. Both options retain multiple actual political/institutional courses and empirical methods; contextual breadth has specific roles. Missing dedicated political projects and research culmination remain major limitations and are not disguised as optional research. Dutch national-institutional depth is not supplied by generic comparative politics, and American media is not relabelled Dutch media politics.
